problem: Game benchmarks lack comprehensive evaluation of LLM capabilities across genres and lack fine-tuning datasets to adapt pre-trained LLMs for gaming agents.
approach: Orak provides a plug-and-play benchmark spanning 12 games across genres, with systematic evaluation of agentic modules and a fine-tuning dataset of expert gameplay trajectories to adapt LLMs into game agents.
contribution: Establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework with leaderboards, battle arenas, and in-depth analysis of input modality and fine-tuning effects for versatile gaming agents.

problem: Time-series foundation models for anomaly detection rely on reconstruction or forecasting error, but these approaches may not accurately detect anomalies.
approach: Critically evaluate five time-series foundation models (MOMENT, Chronos, TimesFM, Time-MoE, TSPulse) against simple baselines like moving-window variance to assess whether foundation models outperform one-liner approaches.
contribution: Demonstrates that anomaly detection performance of foundation models does not significantly differ from simple baselines, revealing fundamental limitations in reconstruction and forecasting-based methodologies.

problem: Existing embedding models lack visual-interactive capabilities to handle localized user intent, preventing entity-level grounding within images.
approach: VIRTUE extends vision-language models with segmentation capabilities to process visual prompts (point, bounding box, mask) for localized entity grounding, and introduces the SCaR benchmark (1M samples) for retrieval of captions with specific objects.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on visual-interactive embedding tasks with entity-level information complementing global representations.

problem: VLA models trained on synthetic data often fail to generalize to real-world robotic manipulation due to the simulation-to-reality gap.
approach: Sim2Real-VLA features a dual-system architecture with a high-level planner inferring object-centered affordance chains and a low-level actor executing plans via tokenized actions, trained exclusively on synthetic data.
contribution: Demonstrates seamless transfer to real-world manipulation across bimanual, dexterous, and long-horizon tasks with improved performance over prior VLA baselines.

problem: Reconstructing transparent objects from multi-view images is challenging due to complex light propagation behavior and constraints to specific scenarios.
approach: DiffTrans proposes a differentiable rendering framework using FlexiCubes for geometry representation and a recursive differentiable ray tracer to optimize geometry, refraction index, and absorption rate end-to-end.
contribution: Achieves high-quality reconstruction of transparent objects in intricate scenes with diverse topology and complex texture.

problem: The Heatmap + MCTS paradigm for TSP emphasizes heatmap sophistication but lacks rigorous evaluation of MCTS configuration impact versus heatmap complexity.
approach: Conduct extensive empirical analysis across diverse TSP scales to assess the relative impact of MCTS strategies versus heatmap complexity, introducing a standardized MCTS hyperparameter tuning pipeline.
contribution: Demonstrates that a simple k-nearest neighbor heatmap with optimally tuned MCTS can match sophisticated learned heatmaps, challenging assumptions about heatmap complexity being the primary performance determinant.

problem: Current LLMs and VLMs struggle with complex multi-modal reasoning over extended contexts, failing on dense information retrieval beyond simple needle-in-haystack tasks.
approach: MMReD benchmark comprises 24 tasks ranging from passkey retrieval to selective/uniform attention across all context chunks to assess dense multi-modal reasoning.
contribution: Reveals consistent performance drops across all tested models as context length increases, with leading reasoning models achieving 0% accuracy on certain tasks at maximum context length of 128 observations.

problem: Video Large Language Models require processing high volumes of visual tokens, causing computational inefficiency when handling videos.
approach: FlashVID uses Attention and Diversity-based Token Selection (ADTS) for representative token selection, then applies Tree-based Spatiotemporal Token Merging (TSTM) for fine-grained redundancy elimination.
contribution: Retaining only 10% of visual tokens preserves 99.1% of LLaVA-OneVision performance; enables 10x increase in video frame input to Qwen2.5-VL with 8.6% relative improvement within same computational budget.

problem: Visual reasoning requires both precise object grounding and spatial relationship understanding; existing methods either demand large-scale supervision or suffer from flawed logic and erroneous grounding.
approach: Proposes annotation-free training using AI-powered verifiers: an LLM verifier refines reasoning via RL, while a VLM verifier strengthens visual grounding through automated hard-negative mining.
contribution: Improves visual reasoning and grounding without ground truth labels, surpassing open-source and proprietary models on diverse spatial reasoning tasks.

problem: LLMs have limited capacity to interpret and design antibodies through natural language due to lack of curated instruction datasets with functional annotations.
approach: AFD-Instruction provides the first large-scale instruction dataset with functional annotations for antibodies, comprising antibody understanding (function inference) and design (de novo generation under constraints).
contribution: Instruction-tuning demonstrates consistent improvements across diverse antibody-related tasks, establishing a foundation for antibody modeling and therapeutic discovery.

problem: Coding agents trained via execution-based feedback suffer from sparse signals that cannot distinguish between successful or unsuccessful trajectories, requiring reliable unit test collection.
approach: SWE-RM develops execution-free reward models that provide fine-grained signals without depending on unit tests; introduces SWE-RM with mixture-of-experts architecture (30B parameters, 3B active).
contribution: Identifies classification accuracy and calibration as crucial for RL training; achieves accurate and robust reward model performance across test-time scaling and reinforcement learning.

problem: GPTQ's assumption of layer-wise independence leads to severe accuracy drops in low-bit quantization regimes; BoA improves this but is substantially less efficient.
approach: TurboBoA introduces three innovations: (i) joint quantization of multiple out-channels with closed-form error compensation for speedup, (ii) correction for errors from preceding layers, (iii) adaptive grid computation with coordinate descent refinement.
contribution: Delivers more than three-fold speedup over BoA while consistently improving accuracy; achieves state-of-the-art results in weight-only and weight-activation quantization.

problem: Video generative models show strong visual generation but lack adherence to physical commonsense in real-world actions, with existing benchmarks suffering from limited size and lack of fine-grained analysis.
approach: VideoPhy-2 curates 4000 diverse prompts and performs human evaluation assessing semantic adherence, physical commonsense, and grounding of physical rules; trains VideoPhy-2-AutoEval for automatic assessment.
contribution: Reveals major shortcomings with best models achieving only 47.7% joint performance on hard subset; models struggle particularly with conservation laws like mass and momentum.

problem: Watermarking provides LLM output provenance but reduces speculative sampling acceptance rate, creating a fundamental trade-off between watermark strength and inference efficiency.
approach: Derive explicit Pareto curves characterizing the trade-off as constrained optimization; introduce mechanism injecting pseudorandomness into draft-token acceptance to maximize watermark strength while maintaining efficiency.
contribution: Breaks the watermark-efficiency trade-off, improving detectability without sacrificing speculative sampling efficiency.

problem: LLMs used in healthcare may worsen existing biases; current methods lack ability to reveal and control spurious reliance on patient race.
approach: Assess Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to reveal associations between race and stigmatizing concepts in gemma-2 models; use SAE latents to steer model outputs for bias mitigation.
contribution: Identifies SAE latents correlating with race; demonstrates that steering via latents can induce problematic associations and offers potential for bias mitigation in controlled settings.

problem: Vision-Language Navigation agents lack fine-grained semantics and physical executability in 3D Gaussian Splatting environments.
approach: SAGE-3D upgrades 3DGS with Object-Centric Semantic Grounding for fine-grained annotations and Physics-Aware Execution Jointing for collision and physical interfaces; introduces InteriorGS dataset (1K scenes) and SAGE-Bench (2M VLN data).
contribution: Demonstrates strong generalizability with 31% improvement on VLN-CE Unseen task; provides benchmark showing 3DGS data is harder to converge but exhibits superior generalization.

problem: LLMs trained with reinforcement learning tend to generate unnecessary and low-quality chain-of-thought steps, failing when initial reasoning direction is suboptimal.
approach: Re² allows LLMs to abandon unproductive reasoning paths and restart via reinforcement learning without preliminary supervised fine-tuning, amplifying redo behavior from 0.5% to over 30%.
contribution: Achieves substantial performance gains over standard RLVR with same training compute budget and notable improvements as test-time samples increase.

problem: Few-shot Whole Slide Image classification suffers from overfitting due to low-dimensional manifold geometry being perturbed by downstream models.
approach: Propose Manifold Residual (MR) block decoupling linear layers into: (1) fixed random matrix as geometric anchor preserving topology, (2) trainable low-rank residual pathway for task-specific adaptation.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art few-shot WSI classification with significantly fewer parameters via geometry-aware learning.

problem: Large Reasoning Models show significant accuracy degradation on long contexts and suffer from over-thinking due to ineffective self-verification.
approach: GrAlgoBench evaluates LRMs on graph algorithm problems allowing fine-grained difficulty control and programmatic verification; comprises nine tasks testing long-context reasoning.
contribution: Reveals accuracy falls below 50% once graphs exceed 120 nodes; demonstrates over-thinking phenomenon driven by extensive yet ineffective self-verification.

problem: Self-Explainable Graph Neural Networks can produce degenerate explanations unrelated to actual model inference, and faithfulness metrics fail to identify these failure modes.
approach: Identify degenerate explanations through empirical analysis; demonstrate that SE-GNNs achieve optimal risk while producing unrelated explanations; introduce novel faithfulness metric reliably marking degenerate explanations.
contribution: Reveals failure modes in SE-GNN explanations and proposes reliable auditing mechanism for both malicious and natural degenerate explanations.

problem: Optimal integration of tools (code, search, reasoning) for diverse questions in tool-augmented LLMs lacks practical guidance.
approach: TUMIX ensemble framework runs multiple agents in parallel with distinct tool-use strategies, iteratively refining responses; enables auto-optimization of agent designs via LLMs.
contribution: Achieves 3.55% accuracy improvement over state-of-the-art on reasoning benchmarks with near-equal inference costs; can halt refinement at confidence targets preserving 49% of inference cost.

problem: Frank-Wolfe algorithms rely on short steps but may not efficiently leverage function smoothness properties for convergence.
approach: Introduce optimistic Frank-Wolfe framework with primal-dual guarantees and generalized short-step strategy optimizing computable primal-dual gap.
contribution: Presents primal-dual convergence proof; empirical results demonstrate optimistic algorithm outperforms existing methods with practical stopping criteria.

problem: Post-training quantization for diffusion LLMs at 2-bit fails to achieve satisfactory performance due to masked-denoising activation patterns differing from standard PTQ assumptions.
approach: Quant-dLLM introduces Masked Calibration Simulation aligning calibration with timestep-dependent masking, Data-aware Any-order Quantizer learning ultra-low-bit representations, and Adaptive Blockwise Mixed Precision for sensitivity-based bit allocation.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art AR-transfer PTQ methods on dLLMs at 2-bit precision.

problem: Data-free continual model merging must balance transparency (avoiding interference with earlier tasks) and fidelity (adapting to new tasks) without task data.
approach: NUFILT proposes null-space filtering to preserve prior responses and lightweight LoRA adapter for task-specific signals, using projection-based surrogate loss.
contribution: Enables backbone to absorb new knowledge while retaining existing behaviors with theoretical subspace alignment guarantees and no extra inference cost.

problem: Electronic structure predictions from quantum mechanical methods are computationally expensive, limiting scalability for practical applications.
approach: BOA introduces Basis Overlap Architecture, an equivariant GNN using novel message passing with overlap matrix of basis functions to predict ground state electron density.
contribution: Surpasses previous state-of-the-art on QM9 and MD density datasets with excellent generalization to larger molecules up to 200 atoms.

problem: Training urban embodied AI agents requires diverse, high-fidelity environments but human-crafted and procedurally generated scenes lack scalability or real-world complexity.
approach: UrbanVerse converts crowd-sourced city-tour videos into physics-aware simulation scenes; provides UrbanVerse-100K (100k+ annotated 3D assets) and UrbanVerse-Gen (automatic pipeline extracting layouts and instantiating scenes).
contribution: Provides 160 high-quality scenes across 24 countries with strong zero-shot sim-to-real transfer improving success by +30.1% and enabling 300 m real-world mission.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization for VLMs relies on oversimplified pairwise comparisons with single negatives, failing to capture complex multimodal preferences.
approach: MISP-DPO incorporates multiple semantically diverse negative images via Plackett-Luce model; selects negatives based on reconstruction difficulty, semantic deviation, and mutual diversity with importance sampling for efficiency.
contribution: Consistently improves multimodal alignment across five benchmarks by incorporating semantic-aware, multi-negative sampling in preference-based learning.

problem: Reduced order modelling for high-dimensional parametric problems using linear subspaces becomes unreliable with classical interpolation in high-dimensional parameter spaces.
approach: Propose neural network-based subspace regression with redundancy strategy (predicting larger-than-needed subspaces) to simplify mapping and reduce complexity.
contribution: Demonstrates significant accuracy improvement with larger subspaces; shows applicability to parametric eigenproblems, deflation, relaxation, optimal control, and PDEs.

problem: LLMs show limited capability for code optimization focused on minimal execution time, with existing methods confined to local improvements.
approach: Adopt problem-oriented perspective reconstructing optimization pairs from multiple programmers on same problem; introduce anchor verification framework to mitigate optimization accuracy trade-offs.
contribution: Significantly enhances both correct optimization ratio and speedup through global algorithmic innovation enabled by problem-centric approach.

problem: Tree-Sliced Wasserstein metric is efficient but computing tree-based p-Wasserstein for p>1 is costly, limiting practical use to p=1 despite higher-order metrics offering better optimization landscapes.
approach: Introduce TS-Sobolev, tree-sliced regularized Sobolev IPM with closed-form expression admitting tractable computation for all p≥1; extends framework to hyperspheres.
contribution: Achieves same computational complexity for p>1 as TSW at p=1 while recovering TSW exactly at p=1; serves as drop-in replacement with additional flexibility.

problem: Real-time super-resolution models struggle with compressed streaming video content; existing datasets do not reflect streaming media characteristics.
approach: Introduce StreamSR dataset from YouTube covering diverse genres and resolutions; benchmark 11 state-of-the-art models; propose EfRLFN with Efficient Channel Attention and hyperbolic tangent activation.
contribution: Demonstrates fine-tuning on StreamSR yields significant performance gains generalizing across standard benchmarks for streaming super-resolution.

problem: Existing code similarity metrics do not reflect algorithmic similarity; LLM-based algorithm design lacks methods to distinguish innovative algorithms from syntactic refinements.
approach: Define algorithm similarity through problem-solving behavior by comparing trajectories of intermediate solutions progressively generated by algorithms.
contribution: Demonstrates utility in improving LLM-based algorithm design via diversity-maintaining search and provides algorithm analysis tool.

problem: Submodular maximization algorithms suffer from prohibitively high computational costs, limiting scalability for practical applications.
approach: Propose AAPGA integrating continuous relaxation, Accelerated Approximate Projected Gradient Ascent, and randomized rounding for near-optimal solutions under cardinality, knapsack, and partition matroid constraints.
contribution: Establishes approximation guarantees with improved query complexity; achieves up to 32.3x speedup over traditional methods on small-scale experiments.

problem: Time series anomaly detection via diffusion models suffers from irreducible variance due to inherent stochasticity, limiting reconstruction fidelity.
approach: ICDiffAD synergizes adaptive noise scheduling via SNR Scheduler with semi-deterministic generation via SNR Implicit Conditioning Mechanism initializing diffusion from partially corrupted inputs.
contribution: Improves F1 score by 20.2% and reduces false positives by 60.23% compared to existing diffusion-based TSAD methods.

problem: Text-to-image generation struggles to faithfully capture user intentions from short, under-specified prompts due to insufficient grounding in visual semantics.
approach: RePrompt introduces reasoning into prompt enhancement via reinforcement learning; trains language model to generate structured, self-reflective prompts optimized for image-level outcomes with tailored reward models.
contribution: Significantly boosts spatial layout fidelity and compositional generalization across diverse T2I backbones, establishing state-of-the-art results on GenEval and T2I-Compbench.

problem: Generative models lack formal verification that they are truly controllable despite proliferation of controlled generation methods.
approach: Provide theoretical framework formalizing controllability as control process; propose algorithm to estimate controllable sets with probably-approximately correct bounds distribution-free for any black-box model.
contribution: Demonstrates model controllability is surprisingly fragile and highly dependent on experimental setting, shifting focus from attempting control to understanding its fundamental limits.

problem: Dataset-level heterogeneity introduces domain biases degrading generalization in Time Series Foundation Models.
approach: FeDaL applies federated learning paradigm to learn dataset-agnostic representations; introduces Domain Bias Elimination (DBE) and Global Bias Elimination (GBE) mechanisms.
contribution: Demonstrates cross-dataset generalization improvements across eight tasks with analysis of federated scaling behavior under decentralization.

problem: Existing associative memory models evaluate retrieval quality based on proximity, which cannot guarantee retrieved patterns have strongest association with query.
approach: Propose adaptive similarity that learns to approximate likelihood of stored patterns generating query from context-drawn samples; integrate into Adaptive Hopfield Network (A-Hop).
contribution: Theoretically proves optimal correct retrieval under noisy, masked, and biased variants; achieves state-of-the-art on memory retrieval, classification, and multiple instance learning.

problem: Feasibility-sensitive QP optimization requires efficient solutions with robustness to both feasible and infeasible problems.
approach: FlexQP provides flexible QP optimizer based on exact constraint relaxation; Deep FlexQP applies deep unfolding to learn dimension-agnostic feedback policies from training data.
contribution: Generalizes to larger dimensions and longer iterations than trained for; outperforms state-of-the-art on portfolio, classification, and regression with PAC Bayes generalization guarantees.

problem: Large Reasoning Models generate excessively long chain-of-thought responses with redundant steps, inflating inference cost while maintaining accuracy remains challenging.
approach: PEAR introduces Phase Entropy Aware Reward mechanism penalizing excessive entropy during thinking phase while allowing exploration in answer phase, enabling adaptive response length control.
contribution: Consistently reduces response length while sustaining competitive accuracy across four benchmarks without explicit length targets or rigid truncation.
